text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN AND SOYBEAN SALE - Egypt bought two 30,000 tonne shipments of yellow corn from Lorico and two 30,000 tonne shipments of soybean from Finagrain, one trader said.
WHEAT SALES - Jordan on Wednesday purchased 100,000 tonnes of Argentine hard red winter wheat at $169.50 per tonne in two equal lots for delivery in March and April.
- The CCC of the USDA said it bought 40,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat for export to Pakistan for February 20-March 15 delivery.

WHEAT SALES - Algeria appeared to have purchased 43,000 tonnes of maize for March 1-10 shipment, but the deal has yet to be confirmed, European grain traders said. Exporters said Algeria on Tuesday might have bought 15,000 tonnes of U.S. maize and 28,000 tonnes of Argentine and/or Brazilian maize.

- Bangladesh has awarded Mitsui & Co a deal for importing 32,250 tonnes of soft red U.S. wheat at $226.81 CIF per tonne for shipment by February 24. Bangladesh is buying the wheat under an 850 million yen Japanese grant. The bidding took place on January 25.
SOYOIL SALE - Strong indications circulated through the U.S. grain industry that China bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil for March shipment on Wednesday, U.S. exporters said.
BARLEY SALES - Malta has bought 6,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley for March shipment at $142.50 per tonne, including C and F, European grain traders said.

- European grain exporters said they were seeking confirmation of market talk that Libya bought optional-origin feed barley. Libya may have bought 200,000 tonnes of barley in bulk and 100,000 tonnes in bags but this was yet to be confirmed. A selling price of $125 per tonne was cited.
WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan will hold side-by-side tenders for 360,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat and Australian white milling wheat, the country's shipping agent said.
Bids for both tenders will be opened on February 16 and must be valid on February 17. Shipment was for March 5-31.
- Egypt will tender Wednesday night for a total of 165,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat in a private tender.

- Iraq will seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on February 11 under the U.N. Food-for-Oil deal, several U.S. exporters said. The tender would be divided into two lots of 25,000 tonnes each, one for April delivery and the other for May.

WHEAT TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade has offered 40,000 tonnes of hard durum amber wheat for sale. An international call set February 12 as the final date for bids had already been issued. Confirmation would be made on February 13.

- Sri Lanka has opened a tender for 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat, for delivery in two lots of hard and soft wheat, an official for the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. The tender, for 50,000 tonnes each of hard and soft wheat, will close on February 7.

BARLEY TENDER - Turkey's state grain board (TMO) canceled a tender to export 150,000 tonnes of feed and 50,000 tonnes of malting barley because of unsatisfactory prices, a TMO official said on Wednesday.

SOYBEAN OIL - The CCC said it would tender February 11 for 11,670 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil under its export program to Peru. The delivery period was slated for March 20 to April 5. The tender was for reply on February 12.
RICE TENDERS - Colombia is preparing to tender for up to 50,000 tonnes of rice to help cover a shortfall in domestic production, Agriculture Ministry sources said.

- Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs has issued an international tender to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment in April. March 3 was set as the final date to receive bids and confirmation would be made on March 12.

MARKET TALK - Uzbekistan will import 1.0-1.2 million tonnes of food wheat this year as its 1996 harvest of 2.7 million tonnes is not enough to cover domestic demand, an official Uzbek grain source said.

... Moroccan traders said the government has imposed new customs duties on soft wheat imports, equivalent to $34 per tonne. The new tax took effect on January 25 and will remain in place until further notice.

... China, currently importing about 100,000 tonnes of soybean oil a month, could step up imports as traders move away from palm oil and new licences to import soybean oil become available, Asian traders said Wednesday.
